chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, all together, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:
'Would that we were a caravan like the family of Yaqoub, until Allah judges between us and His creatures.'

key_terms.آلِ يَعْقُوبَ: The family of Jacob (peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: What does the Imam mean by wishing to be like the family of Yaqoub?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) uses the metaphor of 'travelers' (sayyara) to describe the transient nature of the believers' existence in this world, contrasting their temporary sojourn with the eternal reality of the Hereafter. This narration underscores the Shia concept of *intizar* (waiting for the reappearance) and the patience required while awaiting Allah's final verdict between the righteous and the rest of creation. It reflects the historical context of the Imams' period of concealment and political oppression, where believers were urged to remain steadfast like travelers passing through a foreign land.

en.hubeali: H 14627 – Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father and a number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Yaqoub Bin Yazeed altogether from Hammad Bin Isa, from Ibrahim Bin Umar, from a man, who has narrated the following: Abu Abdullahasws having said:

‘our<sup>asws</sup> matter (treatment of people towards us) is like that of the Children of Yaqoub<sup>as</sup> (towards him<sup>as</sup>) until Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Judges between us<sup>asws</sup> and His<sup>azwj</sup> creatures’.
en.sarwar: 179. Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father and a number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Yaqoub Bin Yazeed altogether from Hammad Bin Isa, from Ibrahim Bin Umar, from a man, who has narrated the following: Abu Abdullah (a.s.) having said:
‘our (a.s.) matter (treatment of people towards us) is like that of the Children of Yaqoub (as) (towards him (as)) until Allah (azwj) Judges between us (a.s.) and His (azwj) creatures’.
